title: A file of the flow set, config/flows/<name>.yaml
description: One file of the flow set (flow-config.md, "Flow files", D-25; F-139 D3). Each file holds flows, subflows, defined steps, step gates and the flow set's settings; `bl` checks the files together as one set after this shape check (F-139 D4, D5). Only the shop writes the flow set (D-85). Each name matches `^[^_/][^/]*$`: a name that starts with `_` is reserved (D-44), and `/` joins box paths (D-37). The `cel` keyword marks each gate condition, each `after` entry and each property, so the load compiles them.

subflows.description: Subflow name → its subflow (flow-config.md, "Subflows are flattened").

defined_steps.description: Defined step name → a code step with its arguments and post-conditions (D-33 to D-35).

step_gates.description: A code step, defined step or subflow name → the gate that holds before it starts (D-38; F-139 Decision A4).

max_box_visits.description: The most starts of one box in one flow invocation (steps.md, "Box visit limit", D-115).

gate_recheck_minutes.description: How often a suspended process checks its gate again (flows.md, "Waking a suspended process", D-21).

Name.description: A flow, subflow, status, box, entry or defined step name: no reserved `_` start (D-44), no `/` (D-37).

initial.description: The status of a new item.

gate.description: The status gate: each entry holds before the item enters the status (D-38).

properties.description: The status properties as conditions over the record (statuses.md, "Status properties", D-64). `closed` is derived from the flow, so no flow writes it.

entries.description: Entry name → where an invocation may start (flows.md, "Entry points", D-48, D-54).

from.description: The statuses the item may hold when the entry starts.

start.description: The box where the invocation starts.

run_states.description: The run states the entry starts from besides `idle` (D-48).

args.description: The option as it is typed → the options of `argparse`'s `add_argument`, with `sets` and `steps` (D-424). F-152 builds their use.

use.description: A code step, a defined step, a subflow, or a shop step as `steps.<name>`; with none, the box runs what its name names.

with.description: The arguments of an inline step; the step's own schema checks them.

use.description: A code step, or a shop step as `steps.<name>`.

with.description: The step's arguments; the step's own schema checks them.

After.description: The post-conditions: each holds after the step returns `success`, or the outcome becomes `failure` (D-35).

Arrow.description: A box name or `stop`, short for `{ next: <name> }`; or an object with exactly one of `next` and `return`, and an optional `status` (D-26, D-43; F-139 Decision A1).

Gate.description: A gate: each entry must give `true` (core.md, "Conditions are CEL").

GateEntry.description: A condition, or `{ condition, class }`, where `class` routes the gated alert.
